about: What the shipped catalog (OBDb public signal definitions) can read about engine-oil condition and service intervals, per vehicle. These are definitions, not measurements: nothing here was read from a vehicle by this research.

generatedFrom.classifiers: MileageSignalClassifier + ServiceMetricClassifier, as compiled in this test run
generatedFrom.note: OBDb-derived tables: CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution and share-alike apply (see README.md).

kinds.OilLifePercent: Remaining life of the oil, in percent. 100 = fresh oil and the value shrinks. OBDb names: 'Oil life remaining', 'Engine oil life remaining', 'Remaining oil life'.
kinds.OilDegradationPercent: Wear of the oil, in percent. 0 = fresh oil and the value GROWS: the opposite scale. OBDb name: 'Engine oil degradation' (service 22, identifier 3813, on the Stellantis / FCA family). Never shown as remaining life and never a reset-to-100 target.
kinds.DistanceToNextService: Distance still to go until the next service or oil change ('Distance to next service', 'Estimated distance to oil change', 'Distance before next oil change').
kinds.DaysToNextService: Days still to go until the next service.
kinds.DistanceSinceOilChange: Distance driven since the last oil change. A counter that grows ('Distance since oil change', 'Mileage since last oil change'). The 'under severe operating conditions' counter of the Stellantis family is a different counter and stays unclassified.
kinds.OilChangeInterval: The configured interval ('Max distance to oil change', 'Oil change interval in km'). A setting, not a counter. Some Renault signals give it in months with the unit 'scalar'.
kinds.MaintenanceCounter: Maintenance items whose meaning is vehicle-specific: Honda / Acura 'Maintenance, <item>' (unit not stated by the definition) and Renault 'Maintenance autonomy ...'. Shown, never interpreted.
kinds.OilLevel: Oil LEVEL (millimetres, percent or a scalar). Not oil life.
kinds.Other: Service-related by name but not one of the above (for example 'Time since last oil change', 'Oil change history 1').

notes: Every oil-life and oil-degradation signal in the catalog is in percent. The scale differs by family: remaining life shrinks, degradation grows.

The Service page's normal refresh sends the non-debug definitions of the exact model and, for oil life, oil degradation, distance and days to service, distance since the oil change and inspection, the identifiers other models of the same make use ('brand-wide'); readings obtained that way carry the research-level evidence label. Other definitions the community flags 'dbg' are sent only on request.

The catalog has no model-year filter (OBDb's 'filter' and 'dbgfilter' did not survive the import), so a row applies to the model whatever the year; a wrong year answers with a negative reply or nothing, and a value is shown only after a positive reply that decodes to a plausible figure.
There is no standard (SAE J1979) PID for oil life or a service interval; the only oil-related standard PID is 5C, engine oil temperature.

Model-year evidence: the catalog keeps one 'debug' flag per row, but OBDb also has 'dbgfilter' (debug in some years only) and 'filter' (the years a command applies to). The app now reads Resources/Raw/obdb_year_evidence.json, derived from OBDb, and for a car with a verified model year uses the flag and the filter of that year and says when OBDb has a recorded reply for it.

A definition whose recorded replies show that it holds something else than its name says is never shown under that name (KnownMislabelledDefinitions): the BMW 'Distance since last oil change' is the odometer.
